Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:193271
Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 879 of 2024
Revisionist :- X- Minor
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Revisionist :- Kapil Kumar,Sandhya Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1-The present criminal revision under Section 102 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 16.12.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/Juvenile Court/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Bulandshahr in Criminal Appeal No. 156 of 2023 ('X' through his legal Guardian/Mother vs. State and Another) and against order dated 31.10.2023 passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Bulandshahr in Case Crime No. 79 of 2023, under section 376-D I.P.C. and Sections 5G/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Ahaar, District Bulandshahr, whereby the learned Juvenile Justice Board as well as learned appellate court refused the prayer of bail of accused-revisionist.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2-Despite service of notice upon the informant, no one has put in appearance on his behalf, hence,
this Court proceeds to hear this matter on its merit.

X- Minor vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125814661/
1 3-Heard learned counsel for the revisionist, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State of U.P. and perused the record.
4-The prosecution case in a nutshell is that the informant-Harkesh, who is father of the victim lodged a first information report on 27.06.2023 with regard to occurrence dated 23.06.2023 against six named accused persons namely Prashant, Neeraj, Jagatveer @ Bhoma, Dharmendra,
Bhanupratap and present revisionist for the offence under Sections 376-D I.P.C. and Sections 5g/6 POCSO Act alleging inter-alia that his son-in-law, namely, Prashant took away his younger daughter, aged about 15 years, to a temple from where he took her away in a forest and committed rape upon her.

F.I.R. also alleges that five other accused persons (including the present revisionist)
have committed rape upon her one by one.

5-Learned counsel for the revisionist, assailing the impugned orders, submits that the revisionist was a juvenile on the date of the alleged incident dated 23.06.2023 and he has been declared juvenile vide order dated 07.08.2023 of Juvenile Justice Board, Bulandshahr treating the age of revisionist as 15 years 02 months and 16 days on the date of alleged incident.

It is next submitted that aforesaid order declaring the revisionist as juvenile has attained finality as the same was never been challenged either by the informant, the averment in this regard has been made in para no. 2 of the supplementary affidavit dated 01.12.2024.
The revisionist has remained confined in juvenile home since 28.06.2023.
6-As to the offence alleged, it is submitted that the revisionist has falsely been implicated in the case with an ulterior motive.
In this regard, it is further stated that proper investigation was not conducted by the police and thus the revisionist had wrongly been charged with the offence.

It is next submitted that co-accused persons, namely, Bhanupratap, Neeraj Kumar and Jagatveer @
Bhoma have been granted bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide orders dated 02.02.2024,
14.03.2024 and 15.04.2024 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 50778 of 2023, 53854 of 2023 and 7653 of 2024 respectively.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 50778 of 2023, 53854 of 2023 and 7653 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 7-It is further being emphasized that the revisionist does not have any criminal antecedent to his credit.

Lastly, it is submitted that there is no material on record for believing that the release of revisionist is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal or expose him to moral,
psychological danger, therefore, aforesaid impugned orders are not sustainable and liable to be set aside and revisionist is entitled to be released on bail in view of Section 12 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015.
8

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: -Learned Additional Government Advocate vehemently opposed the present revision.
It has thus been submitted, merely because the revisionist is a juvenile it would not entitle him to bail without going into the gravity of the offence, the nature of the crime.
It is also contended that the bail sought for has been rightly refused in view of Section 12(1) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Child) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
9-Having considered the arguments so advanced by learned counsel for the parties, it is true that a juvenile offender is not entitled as of right to be enlarged on bail, irrespective of any other fact or X- Minor vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125814661/
2 circumstance, however, it also cannot be denied that in view of specific and special legislative intent and intervention, refusal of bail in the case of a juvenile may be made only for specific reasons and circumstance.

Otherwise, a general legislative presumption does appear to exist under the scheme of the Act that the welfare of alleged juvenile offender would be better served without he being confined for long duration.
Here, the revisionist has remained in juvenile home since 28.06.2023 against the maximum sentence of three years in case of conviction.

The allegation against all the accused persons are same and three of them have been granted bail, as noted above, therefore case of the revisionist stands on similar footing than that of co-accused persons.

10-The Court has to see whether the opinion of the learned appellate Court as well as Juvenile Justice Board recorded in the impugned judgment and orders are in consonance with the provision of Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Section 12 of the aforesaid Act lays down three contingencies in which bail could be refused to juvenile.

They are:-
(i) if the release is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal, or (ii) expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger, or (iii) that his release would defeat the ends of justice.
11-Gravity of the offence has not been mentioned as a ground for rejection of bail in Section 12 of the aforesaid Act.

Though the prayer for bail of the revisionist has been opposed by learned counsel for the opposite State, but could not demonstrate from the record that there existed any of the grounds on which bail application of a juvenile could be rejected keeping in view the provisions of Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice Act.
12-Considering the above, it appears that the findings recorded by the learned Court below are erroneous and cannot be sustained.
The aforesaid impugned orders dated 16.12.2023 and 31.10.2023 are hereby set aside.
13-Accordingly, the present criminal revision is allowed.
The revisionist through guardian shall remain present before the trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence,
without sufficient cause, the trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

Order Date :- 10.12.2024 Saurabh  X- Minor vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125814661/
